html:
SMTO-TSK-0016 — This action points to a task in a different place

GUID: e756760e-66e7-49d0-ad03-c6a870a16139
Slug: task-scope-mismatch
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to act on a task, conversation or computer that doesn't belong to the work in front of you. To avoid acting on the wrong thing, it refused. Nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page, then open the conversation from the Conversations pane. An out-of-date page can send a task from one conversation together with another conversation.
  2. If you were branching, select Continue in new conversation on the reply of the task you want, inside the conversation you are viewing. Click it only once. A branch must start from a task in the same conversation, and each click counts as a separate request.
  3. If this appeared while the Agent was working, check Gateways for this prompt in the message box and make sure the computer you want is selected, then send your request again. The Agent can only run work on the Gateways (helper programs on your computers) chosen for that task.

What success looks like

  • The branch opens, or the task runs on the computer you selected, without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't copy task links or IDs from one conversation into another to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A request's task, conversation or activity reference does not match the scope it is bound to: a branch request or submission ID belongs to another task or conversation, or a parallel target or Activity reference falls outside the run's selected Gateways or known activities.

What this means

  • Fork/submission/conversation identity differs from its saved binding, or an activity target/reference is outside the accepted current scope. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Fork/submission/conversation identity differs from its saved binding, or an activity target/reference is outside the accepted current scope.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare source conversation/request bindings and selected activity/Gateway scope; do not borrow another task's authority.

How to fix it

  • Compare the identifiers in Technical details with the current scope: a task fork must use a request_id owned by the given conversation and a fresh client_submission_id per click; native state initialization must match its request's conversation; parallel targets must be within the run's named Gateway scope; Activity references must name an existing activity of this run. Use the correct identity rather than re-targeting saved work.
  • Use the exact task, conversation and selected-target references belonging to the intended current scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended action uses identities and targets owned by its accepted scope.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
